title: Fix scheduler tick drift causing queue accumulation & long-context tail latency
creator: Maya Patel
description: Several customers (hosted + Dedicated tenants) reported recurring long-context tail latency spikes coincident with multi-hour ingress patterns. Investigation shows scheduler tick timestamps on a subset of nodes drifted relative to the central admission clock, causing periodic backlog accumulation and delayed batch formation for long-context requests. This ticket tracks the analysis, hotfix, rollout, and validation for a portable fix that covers Hosted, Dedicated pools, and Private deployments.
incident_summary: Starting 2026-03-02 customers observed 95th/99th token latency increases by 2-5x for runs that included long-context (>=16k) requests interleaved with small short requests. Symptoms: growing queue depth, delayed admission of latency-sensitive small requests once tick alignment slipped. The issue was reproducible in staging by introducing small clock skew on a subset of scheduler nodes.
root_cause_analysis: Root cause: A timer drift in the per-instance admission tick (caused by a missed NTP sync during a maintenance window) allowed some nodes to under-report their contribution to the admission reservoir. The admission controller uses tick intervals to age tokens and refill admission budgets; drifted nodes would not release admission fast enough, causing neighboring healthy nodes to absorb unexpected load and creating backlog amplification for long-context requests. Secondary cause: a recent change to the admission smoothing heuristic reduced hysteresis, making the system less tolerant to transient tick jitter.
mitigation_notes: Short-term mitigations applied: (1) Emergency config rollback of admission smoothing change (PR #14822) to restore hysteresis; (2) forced NTP resync and drift monitoring script deployed to affected pools; (3) temporary routing rule to prefer nodes with healthy tick metrics for latency-sensitive routes. These reduced tail spikes within 30 minutes for the impacted tenants.
updates: 2026-03-05 - Maya Patel: Escalation opened after PagerDuty alerts and customer Slack threads. Collected stack traces, admission metrics, and confirmed correlation with tick skew reports from node telemetry.

2026-03-06 - Lucas Rivera: Reproduced behavior in staging by injecting a 120-400ms tick delay on 20% of scheduler replicas. Captured queue depth, admission budget per-node, and per-route latency traces. Created perf profile showing backlog growth at 60s horizon.

2026-03-07 - Lucas Rivera: Drafted hotfix: add tick-drift-detection and local compensated-ageing (PR runtime-14845). Hotfix increases local ageing when drift detected and adds a metric 'tick_drift_seconds' with alert threshold. Requesting review from runtime leads.

2026-03-09 - Runtime team review: Feedback from Priya Shah to tighten unit tests for admission window and add deterministic simulation for mixed-length workloads. Also asked to include config gating and feature-flag for private deployments.

2026-03-11 - Lucas Rivera: Addressed reviews, added e2e simulation harness (github.com/redwood/runtime/sim) inputs to reproduce mixed-length arrival patterns. Updated PR to include opt-in flag 'enable_tick_compensation' default off for Private customers until validated.

2026-03-12 - Ops: Deployed hotfix to canary pool in Hosted with feature flag enabled and routed two escalated customers for validation. Monitored 1h of production traffic: 95th/99th token latency dropped 40% for previously impacted windows. No regressions observed in throughput.

2026-03-14 - Lucas Rivera: Opening this Linear ticket for rollout planning to Dedicated and Private customers. Remaining tasks: finalize telemetry dashboards, add automated repair (auto-resync) for NTP drift, and produce communication notes for affected customers.
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix merged and smoke-tested in staging with feature flagged rollout
Canary deployment in Hosted shows >=30% reduction in 95/99 token latency for previous incident windows
Dedicated and Private rollout plan documented with opt-in gating for Private clusters
Monitoring: new dashboards for tick_drift_seconds, per-node admission budget, and automated alerts configured
Post-rollout runbook created and on-call briefed
rollout_plan: Step 1: Merge runtime-14845 after final approvals
Step 2: Canary in Hosted (10% capacity) with flag on for escalated customers — 24h observation
Step 3: Gradual Hosted ramp to 100% over 48h if metrics stable
Step 4: Coordinate Dedicated customer migrations during maintenance windows; apply hotfix + NTP auto-resync script
Step 5: For Private customers, deliver patch + opt-in flag and provide operator instructions and KMS-signed bundle
Step 6: Run 7-day heat-monitoring and close ticket after stability window
postmortem_tasks: Deploy automated NTP healthcheck and auto-repair across all pools
Reintroduce improved admission smoothing with canary-safe thresholds
Add deterministic scheduler-sim test to CI for mixed-length interleaving patterns
Run a 72h chaos test simulating clock jitter and verify no tail amplification
Customer communications: send incident summary + mitigation steps to affected accounts
